source.title: Successor Heads: Recurring, Interpretable Attention Heads In The Wild
source.authors: Rhys Gould; Euan Ong; George Ogden; Arthur Conmy

record.tranche_reason: Tests for interpretable features in language models, including whether sparse-autoencoder features capture recurring numeric structure; this extends the claim's feature-representation question to LLMs rather than reproducing the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own measurements and interventions on SAE features, probes, and MLP0 neurons relevant to V4. The paper's results about successor-head polysemantic behavior do not test capacity pressure or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly about successor heads. It still tests V4 in a new setting. It trains SAEs on Pythia-1.4B MLP0 outputs and recovers mod-10 features. It then asks whether these are SAE artifacts, checking them against a linear probe, individual neuron ablations, causal OV-circuit logits and vector-arithmetic steering. This bears on whether LLMs contain sparse features an SAE can recover, and whether those features are spread across neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is incomplete. The authors' main conclusion concerns successor heads, which increment ordinal tokens. They report these heads across GPT-2, Pythia and Llama-2 from 31M to 12B parameters, as evidence of weak universality. They find the heads read compositional numeric representations containing abstract mod-10 features. The heads reduce loss on succession examples in training data. Additional findings are a greater-than bias, surprisingly interpretable MLP0 neurons, and a polysemantic head that also predicts acronyms. They acknowledge that the mod-10 features miss the greater-than bias and fail on days and letters.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes trained language models using effective OV circuits, SAEs, probes, neuron ablations, and vector edits; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature behavior varies by task: mod-10 features do not interpret or steer the day and letter tasks well, and vector arithmetic performs differently across months and digits 20–29. Arithmetic also works worse when the mod-10 addition is smaller than the source value modulo 10.

fits_no_version.finding: Successor head L12H0 in Pythia-1.4B is 'interpretably polysemantic'. It performs successorship (43.4% of winning cases), acronym (23.8%) and greater-than (18.9%) behaviours, in overlapping rather than disjoint contexts. The authors call this surprising given superposition research.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention heads in LLMs can be polysemantic across distinct, co-occurring interpretable functions.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (venue metadata); the text labels this version preprint, under review.
record.problems: The detailed SAE case study centers on Pythia-1.4B, with only qualitative SAE plots for additional models. Some results are figure-based without reported numerical values. The authors report task failures for days and letters and note that the mod-10 feature account misses aspects such as the greater-than bias.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable reported result was left out. The paper's compositionality projection results and natural-language successor-head behavior were not extracted because they do not directly measure the feature-distribution or SAE-recovery claims in V4.

untested.parts: No toy models; no sparsity-dependent transition or geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity comes from capacity competition.
Reports a polysemantic attention head, but does not test capacity pressure or non-capacity causes of polysemantic neurons.
SAE features are averaged over 100 runs, and hyperparameters were chosen by cross-run mean max cosine similarity. No stability or completeness figures are reported, and canonicity is not tested.
Dimensionality of features is not examined.

missing.what: Head-level polysemanticity proportions: winning cases (successorship 43.4%, acronym 23.8%, greater-than 18.9%) and loss-reducing shares under several ablation methods

record.verdict_notes: SAE analysis covers only MLP0 of Pythia-1.4B in detail. The 'similar mod-10 features in all cases' claim is backed by SAE plots for only two additional models, not Llama. The SAE training data was dominated by number tokens. Vector-arithmetic rates are conditional on the added residue exceeding the source residue. The individual-neuron interpretability result somewhat cuts against the view that features are spread across many neurons.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, feature overlap and geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by competition for limited capacity or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity can arise for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether it is evidence for superposition.
The study analyzes particular numeric features and tasks; it does not establish how widespread feature spreading or SAE-recoverable features are across LLMs generally.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable across methods or settings, or canonical units of model representation.
The study does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features or test the dimensionality of the model's underlying features.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Trained SAEs on MLP0 representations and identified the modal most-important feature for each mod-10 class across 100 SAE training runs.

conditions.value: numeric tokens grouped by index modulo 10

rows.measure: Average proportion of tokens in a mod-10 class sharing that class's modal most-important SAE feature
rows.note: The authors report that the most-important feature is shared on average by 58.5% of tokens in each mod-10 class.
rows.check: The modal most-important feature is shared by only 58.5% of tokens in each mod-10 class on average, so the recovery is clear but incomplete. 'Partial' fits better than 'observed'. Baseline: none stated.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Applied the successor head's effective OV circuit to each mod-10 feature.
rows.measure: Whether the resulting logits favor tokens whose index is one greater modulo 10
rows.value: The logit distribution places high weight on tokens tj for j ≡ i + 1 (mod 10) when applying the head to feature fi.
rows.note: The text describes the result; the plotted logits are not reported as numerical values.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Compared a linear probe's mod-10 directions with the corresponding SAE features.

conditions.value: 10 mod-10 probe directions and SAE features

rows.measure: Average cosine similarity between each probe row and its corresponding SAE feature
rows.note: The probe directions correspond to SAE features, but the reported average cosine is below 1.
rows.check: An average cosine of 0.71 between an independently trained probe and the SAE features is high agreement in d_model space. The authors offer it as evidence the features are not SAE artifacts. A cosine below 1 is not by itself a partial result.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Trained a linear probe on numeric tokens to predict index modulo 10 and tested it on tokens from other succession tasks.
rows.measure: Correct mod-10 predictions on unseen non-numeric-task examples
rows.note: The eight failures listed include January, December, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, V, X, and XV.
rows.check: This measures generalisation of a linear probe to non-numeric tokens (94/102). It shows a linear mod-10 direction exists, but it is not SAE recovery and not a measure of how features are spread across neurons. No SAE is involved.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated individual MLP0 neurons and examined the activations and successor logits of the most important neurons for numeric-token incrementation.
rows.measure: Periodic firing patterns among important neurons and their contribution to successor logits
rows.value: The most common firing period across the top 16 most important neurons was 10; the authors also state that feature f6 appears in superposition across at least two neurons.
rows.note: The paper describes periodic firing and successor-logit increases, but does not provide a numerical count of neurons with period 10.
rows.check: Of the top 16 MLP0 neurons, the most common firing period is 10, and individual neurons are described as surprisingly interpretable. Only f6 is said to be in superposition, across at least two neurons. This is weak evidence of features spread across many neurons.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Added and subtracted mod-10 SAE feature vectors to change a token representation's index, then evaluated the successor head's logits.
rows.measure: Fraction of cases where the edited representation placed maximal logits on the target successor
rows.note: The authors say the arithmetic works when the mod-10 addition is larger than the source value modulo 10; performance is worse for decrementation.
rows.check: The 53% rate applies only to cases where the added residue exceeds the source residue. Arithmetic works much worse in the other cases (greater-than bias), so the overall success rate is lower.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Added and subtracted mod-10 SAE feature vectors to change a token representation's index, then evaluated the successor head's logits.
rows.measure: Fraction of cases where the edited representation placed maximal logits on the target successor
rows.note: The paper reports this rate for cases where the mod-10 addition is larger than the source value modulo 10.
rows.check: The 89% rate is conditional: only cases where the added residue exceeds the source residue. Decrementation cases mostly fail; for example, a '+10' effect appears in 2/3 of below-diagonal entries.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Examined whether mod-10 feature logits form interpretable patterns across the succession tasks.
rows.measure: Whether mod-10 feature logits show an interpretable pattern for the task
rows.value: The mod-10 features were not very interpretable for days in terms of logits; there was no clear diagonal of high logits.
rows.note: The paper also states that the mod-10 features are not able to steer the Days task.
rows.check: The SAE was trained on data dominated by number tokens, so this is a transfer failure of number-derived features, not a failure of an SAE trained on days.

source_check.correct: For V4, state=cannot_determine. Number-derived mod-10 features show no clear day-task logit pattern and cannot steer Days; recovery of day-specific features is not established or ruled out.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.4, limitations; Appendices A.2 and E; Figure 17
source_check.problem: Absent describes transfer performance, not absence of SAE-recoverable features under V4.

rows.subject: EleutherAI/pythia-2.8b
rows.operation_detail: Applied the paper's SAE analysis to numeric-token MLP0 representations and displayed mod-10 feature activations and logits.
rows.measure: Presence of mod-10 feature activation and logit patterns
rows.value: The paper states that it observed mod-10 structure via SAEs across models; plots are provided for this model.
rows.note: No numerical performance value is stated for this model.
rows.check: Qualitative plots only, with no number. SAE hyperparameters were not retuned for this model.

relationships.condition: Pythia-1.4B MLP0 number tokens; Pythia-2.8B and celebrimbor-gpt2-medium (qualitative plots)
relationships.reason: An SAE recovers mod-10 features (r1). These features match an independent probe (r3), causally drive successor logits (r2) and steer number tokens well (r7). The same structure appears in two other models (r10, r11).
relationships.display_finding: An SAE recovered mod-10 features that matched an independent probe, causally drove successor logits and steered number tokens well. The same structure appeared in the two other models.

source_check.condition: Pythia-1.4B MLP0 number tokens; Pythia-2.8B and celebrimbor-gpt2-medium (qualitative plots)
source_check.reason: SAEs recover mod-10 features; independent probe agreement and successor-circuit interventions substantiate their relevance. Appendix A.3 reports similar structure in the two additional models.

relationships.condition: Transfer to other tasks and steering, and how features are distributed across neurons, in Pythia-1.4B
relationships.reason: The mod-10 features fail to interpret or steer days and letters (r8, r9), and steering works for only 53% of month cases even under favourable conditions (r6). Features are largely carried by individual period-10 neurons, with only f6 shown across two neurons (r5).
relationships.display_finding: The mod-10 features failed to interpret or steer days and letters, and steering worked for only 53% of month cases even under favourable conditions. The features were largely carried by individual period-10 neurons, with only one feature (f6) shown across two neurons.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Transfer to other tasks and steering, and how features are distributed across neurons, in Pythia-1.4B
source_check.reason: Justified narrowly by r5 as a qualification of the many-neurons wording: individual neurons can be interpretable, while f6 spans at least two neurons. The transfer and steering failures qualify number-derived feature reuse, not SAE recoverability; the text does not establish that most features align with single neurons.

relation.reason: Its own SAE, probe and neuron experiments bear on V4, beyond merely using or citing superposition.

tranche.reason: Reports SAE-recovered numeric features and independent mechanistic evidence in trained language models, a new setting relative to the original toy models.

source_check.notes: The 53% and 89% rates apply only when the added residue exceeds the source residue, as the row notes acknowledge. The SAE training data include other ordinal tasks but are dominated by numbers; day/letter transfer failures do not test completeness of task-specific SAE recovery.

reader_labels.reason: SAE analysis identifies recurring mod-10 features, the successor head maps them toward successor residues, and probe and neuron analyses provide additional evidence for related structure (r1–r5, r10–r11).
